result.label: bug
result.what_to_change: In handleClick, the promise chain only calls setBusy(false) in the .then() success branch; add a .catch (or use try/finally) around exportReport so that setBusy(false) runs (and an error toast is shown) when the export fails, instead of leaving busy stuck true and the button/select permanently disabled.
result.evidence: handleClick does `exportReport(reportId, format).then(() => { setBusy(false); toast.show(...) })` with no catch/finally; exportReport() throws an Error when res.ok is false, so a failed export rejects the promise and setBusy(false) is never called, leaving disabled={busy} true on both the select and button until the page reloads.

not_searched: other components that might also trigger exports (e.g. bulk export UI)

text: Found it — `handleClick` only resets `busy` and shows toast on success; there's no `.catch`/`.finally`, so a rejected promise (failed export) leaves `busy` stuck `true` forever, keeping the button and format selector disabled.

text: Finding submitted: the bug is in `src/components/ExportButton.tsx`, where `handleClick` lacks error handling on the `exportReport` promise, leaving `busy` (and thus the disabled button) stuck true after a failed export.

input.title: Re-enable the export button after a failed export
input.body:
File: src/components/ExportButton.tsx

handleClick's promise chain only calls setBusy(false) in the success (.then) branch, so a rejected exportReport() call (thrown when res.ok is false) leaves busy stuck true and the select/button permanently disabled. Add a .catch (or wrap in try/finally) so setBusy(false) runs on failure too, and show an error toast in that path.
